meta.scope: Production-grade audit and remediation plan for the Milking Monitor platform
meta.auditor_role: Senior software engineer with systems architecture background
meta.objective: Transform the current platform from a strong prototype into a resilient, secure, operable, production-ready monitoring system for real dairy operations.

executive_summary.overall_assessment: Strong technical foundation with clear separation of concerns, good domain modeling, and a thoughtful event-driven design. The system has the right architectural skeleton for production, but it is still missing the hardening required for operational reliability, secure deployment, predictable ML behavior, and true multi-site scale.
strengths: Clear service split between web app, inference service, and stream layer
Good use of event-driven architecture between backend services
Domain model matches the operational workflow: sessions -> cow processes -> task events
Operational concepts already included such as session lifecycle, stop conditions, and watchdogs
Separation of training assets and runtime service is sensible for a research-driven project
gaps: Single active-session limitation reduces production scalability
ML pipeline still relies on rule-based task logic and may be unstable under real-world noise
Security and auth hardening are not fully production-grade
Observability, tracing, and alerting are not yet mature enough for 24/7 operations
Deployment strategy is not clearly production-safe for multi-camera or multi-site operations
Data integrity and lifecycle guarantees need stronger business rules and idempotency
executive_summary.recommended_target_state: A production system with deterministic session orchestration, robust pipeline monitoring, well-defined ML thresholds, secure authentication, resilient deployment, and auditable operational data.

production_readiness_ranking.comment: Good foundation, but needs multi-session support, explicit contract boundaries, and operational guardrails.
Session lifecycle and watchdog logic exist, but resilience under stream loss, model failure, and DB jitter needs improvement.
Bearer-token auth exists, but broader security posture must be hardened for real-world use.
The ML approach is credible but not yet robust enough for production-grade compliance detection across real farm conditions.
Good initial logging, but lacking full telemetry, traceability, and alerting.
The event model is promising and auditable, but idempotency and validation rules need tightening.
Docker setup is sound for local development, but not yet robust for secure production deployment.

recommended_modifications.title: Introduce a production session orchestration layer with multi-camera and multi-session support
recommended_modifications.current_issue: The inference service only allows a single active session at a time, which is not enough for a real production deployment with multiple stream sources, farms, or concurrent monitoring windows.
recommended_changes: Replace the ad-hoc active-runner registry with a durable session scheduler with explicit queueing and concurrency controls.
Model each camera stream as a resource with lifecycle management: idle, starting, active, degraded, stopped, failed.
Allow multiple sessions per deployment, with resource limits tied to CPU/GPU capacity and camera count.
Define a policy for session conflict resolution: reject, queue, or preempt depending on farm priority.
Add a SessionCoordinator service that owns any active session state, rather than depending solely on in-memory runtime tracking.
acceptance_criteria: Multiple camera sessions can be started under configured concurrency limits.
The scheduler rejects or queues sessions cleanly when resources are exhausted.
A session failure does not corrupt another running session's state.

recommended_modifications.title: Separate domain contracts from transport contracts and enforce API versioning
recommended_modifications.current_issue: The system currently conflates inference event payloads and web app internal database contracts. This makes extension and compatibility harder over time.
recommended_changes: Define explicit event schemas in a shared contract package or registry.
Version all inference payloads and dashboard APIs, e.g. v1 and v2.
Introduce explicit event types: session.started, session.completed, cow_process.started, cow_process.completed, task.detected, task.missed, task.overridden.
Validate schemas centrally in both inference and web layers before processing.
Document compatibility guarantees and deprecation policy.
acceptance_criteria: All producer/consumer payloads are versioned and validated.
Rejecting unsupported payload versions fails with clear diagnostics.
Backward compatibility is documented for at least one minor release cycle.

recommended_modifications.title: Add robust stream health monitoring, failover, and retry policies
recommended_modifications.current_issue: The runtime assumes the RTSP stream is healthy; there is no strong detection of camera outage, stale frames, no-data state, or automatic recovery.
recommended_changes: Track stream freshness: frames per second, stale frame age, decode errors, and latency.
If the stream is stale for a threshold, mark the session as degraded and trigger a failover to a backup stream or fallback video.
Add operator-visible camera health status in dashboard and alerts.
Add bounded retry logic with exponential backoff for inference submission and external calls.
Implement graceful degradation when detection cannot run rather than silently continuing with stale state.
acceptance_criteria: A disconnected camera causes a clear degraded state and alert.
The system recovers cleanly after a transient outage.
Session data shows whether the stream was healthy or degraded at a given time.

recommended_modifications.title: Strengthen idempotency, event persistence, and replay safety
recommended_modifications.current_issue: The system publishes events, but uses in-memory assumptions and lacks explicit deduplication or replay protection. This is risky in the presence of restarts or duplicate deliveries.
recommended_changes: Add idempotency keys per event type and session so duplicate event delivery is harmless.
Persist event receipts or processing ledger entries in the database to prevent duplicate task writes.
Use upsert logic for task updates rather than blindly appending duplicates.
Mark events with a source, event_uuid, and processed_at timestamp.
Provide an event replay/recovery worker for missed or partially processed event batches.
acceptance_criteria: Duplicate events do not create duplicate task records.
Replayed events produce deterministic state.
The dashboard reflects the same task state after a service restart.

recommended_modifications.title: Harden authentication, authorization, and secret management
recommended_modifications.current_issue: The system has token-based ingestion auth, but production security needs stronger identity, environment isolation, and privileged-action boundaries.
recommended_changes: Move to secret manager integration for production, not .env-only secrets.
Using NextAuth and Drizzle is good, but add role-based access controls for supervisor vs admin vs viewer roles.
Protect all privileged endpoints with explicit permission checks in addition to token validation.
Use short-lived signed tokens or session-based auth for internal service calls where possible.
Restrict CORS and network exposure to explicitly trusted origins and internal services.
acceptance_criteria: Unprivileged users cannot access supervisor or admin APIs.
No credentials are committed to the repository or environment files in production.
A production deployment enforces least privilege for all services.

recommended_modifications.title: Protect inference and web endpoints with layered security controls
recommended_modifications.current_issue: The current web ingest route validates payloads and tokens, but the platform needs stronger API hygiene for real deployments.
recommended_changes: Add HTTP security headers for all responses.
Add request signing or mutual TLS for internal service-to-service communication when operating beyond local networks.
Add audit logging for all privileged operations: overrides, status changes, session edits, report generation, and user access.
Rate-limit by service identity and apply WAF style protections for public endpoints.
Sanitize any user-provided content before storage and display.
acceptance_criteria: All public HTTP endpoints return security headers.
Sensitive actions are logged and attributable to a person or service.
Payload sanitation is unit-tested for attack vectors.

recommended_modifications.title: Strengthen the persistence model with explicit database invariants
recommended_modifications.current_issue: The data model is good, but not yet strict enough for high-integrity operational data. Without clear invariants, duplicate or contradictory states can be stored.
recommended_changes: Add database constraints to enforce valid task IDs, status values, and session link integrity.
Add CHECK constraints for allowed statuses and valid time ranges.
Track session status transitions in a state table or audit log with transition validation.
Enforce that detected_start_time <= detected_end_time where applicable.
Add proper indexes on session_id, cow_position, status, created_at, and task_id.
acceptance_criteria: Database rejects malformed status transitions and invalid event times.
Session queries are performant even with large historical datasets.
Data integrity errors are surfaced as explicit operational alerts.

recommended_modifications.title: Create a canonical audit trail and event provenance model
recommended_modifications.current_issue: The current audit-log concept is promising but still needs more strict event provenance for all modifications and decisions.
recommended_changes: Standardize all state changes as immutable events with actor, reason, old_state, new_state, timestamp, and source.
Capture override actions, system auto-marks, and any manual corrections with no ambiguity.
Link audit records to both session and task-event IDs.
Expose an audit view to supervisors for investigation and compliance review.
acceptance_criteria: Every override and state transition is traceable to a human or system actor.
Historical decisions can be reconstructed without ambiguity.
Compliance review screens show a trustworthy change log.

recommended_modifications.title: Replace heuristic-only task detection with a production-grade validation pipeline
recommended_modifications.current_issue: The current logic is explainable but still brittle in the face of occlusion, moving personnel, changing farm layout, and noisy camera conditions.
recommended_changes: Train and validate a farm-specific detector using labeled milking data from actual facility conditions.
Add calibration and threshold tuning using real-world validation sets and confusion matrices.
Introduce per-task confidence ranges with time-based smoothing, not single-threshold decisions.
Add human review workflows for low-confidence tasks and unverified detections.
Measure precision/recall by task and by position rather than just aggregate score.
acceptance_criteria: Task precision and recall are measured against a labeled benchmark dataset.
Low-confidence states trigger review rather than silent auto-completion.
The system performs reliably under realistic farm noise and motion conditions.

recommended_modifications.title: Introduce model quality monitoring and drift detection
recommended_modifications.current_issue: The platform lacks explicit quality controls for model drift, data distribution shift, and silent degradation over time.
recommended_changes: Track detection distribution and confidence drift over time.
Flag scenarios where the observed class frequency or task completion rate deviates from expected values.
Create a model-health dashboard for operators and ML owners.
Retain a benchmark validation set and run periodic revalidation on new data.
Define escalation rules for suspicious performance drops.
acceptance_criteria: Model quality metrics are visible in a monitoring dashboard.
Drift alerts are generated automatically when thresholds exceed baseline.
Operational teams can tell when a model requires retraining or recalibration.

recommended_modifications.title: Add structured telemetry, tracing, and centralized logs
recommended_modifications.current_issue: There is basic logging, but no production-grade observability stack or correlation across service boundaries.
recommended_changes: Add structured JSON logging in both web and inference services.
Add request tracing with correlation IDs across HTTP calls and internal events.
Emit metrics for frame rate, inference latency, event volume, task completion rate, and error counts.
Integrate with a centralized log aggregator such as OpenTelemetry, ELK, or a managed telemetry platform.
Add service dashboards for CPU, memory, latency, errors, and throughput.
acceptance_criteria: Every request and session lifecycle event carries a trace or correlation ID.
Ops can identify the root cause of a degraded inference session from logs and metrics.
A production operator can diagnose service health in under 5 minutes.

recommended_modifications.title: Add alerting and incident playbooks for operational events
recommended_modifications.current_issue: The project includes dashboards and reports but not a mature operational alerting model for failures, stale streams, or abnormal task patterns.
recommended_changes: Define alerts for camera stream loss, inference service crash, DB outage, high task miss rate, and suspicious anomaly clusters.
Create runbooks for each alert with clear remediation steps.
Add alert routing via email, SMS, or incident channel for critical events.
Separate severity levels: critical, warning, informational.
acceptance_criteria: Critical operational issues trigger immediate notifications.
Alerts include enough context to diagnose and act quickly.
Every alert has an associated playbook or runbook.

recommended_modifications.title: Use a production deployment model with immutable infrastructure and environment separation
recommended_modifications.current_issue: The compose setup is fine for local development but not a production deployment model for reliability, security, or scaling.
recommended_changes: Adopt a production deployment stack such as Docker Swarm, Kubernetes, or a managed container platform.
Separate dev, staging, and production environments with isolated config and secrets.
Use immutable container builds and versioned releases.
Add health checks, rolling updates, and graceful shutdown semantics for all services.
Standardize environment variables and config via a secure config management strategy.
acceptance_criteria: Production deploys are isolated from dev and staging state.
Service upgrades are zero-downtime or have defined rollback procedures.
All environment config is tracked and approved through a release pipeline.

recommended_modifications.title: Implement automated CI/CD with quality gates and release verification
recommended_modifications.current_issue: The repository appears to have workflow and build scaffolding, but production-grade release discipline needs validation gates that catch integration failures before deployment.
recommended_changes: Add linting, formatting, type-checking, unit tests, integration tests, and model validation to CI.
Block deployments when smoke tests or build health checks fail.
Include contract tests for the inference-to-web event interface.
Add staging environment smoke tests before promoting to production.
Require artifact signing or provenance for release builds.
acceptance_criteria: No merge reaches production without passing quality gates.
Exposing a broken inference contract is caught automatically.
Smoke tests validate the platform in a production-like environment.

recommended_modifications.title: Increase test coverage with end-to-end and contract tests for the real domain workflow
recommended_modifications.current_issue: The project includes tests, but production reliability requires validating the full operational sequence: camera input -> task detection -> event ingestion -> dashboard updates -> reporting.
recommended_changes: Add end-to-end tests for a full milking session lifecycle with synthetic video input.
Create contract tests for the inference service event JSON schema.
Test session start, stop, timeout, and completion transitions explicitly.
Expand tests for missed-task logic and override behavior.
Run regression tests against known edge-case scenarios such as occlusion and stream interruption.
acceptance_criteria: Critical flows are covered by automated tests with clear pass/fail evidence.
Session lifecycle transitions are validated end-to-end.
Regression fixes are easy to verify before release.

recommended_modifications.title: Refine the operator workflow for high-stakes monitoring scenarios
recommended_modifications.current_issue: The dashboard is strong as a prototype but should be optimized for real farm operations where users need clarity, speed, and low cognitive load under stress.
recommended_changes: Reduce noise in live monitoring screens and emphasize current task status, anomalies, and required actions.
Provide operator-friendly visual states for degraded camera, missed tasks, and override review.
Add keyboard shortcuts and focused workflows for high urgency actions.
Improve the scheduler, session detail, and reporting UX for real farm administrators.
Ensure the UI remains usable in low-light or high-traffic operational conditions.
acceptance_criteria: Operators can identify a problem in seconds without scanning multiple screens.
The UI clearly separates informational alerts from actionable compliance problems.
The workflow is stable and readable even during times of operational pressure.

recommended_modifications.title: Make compliance reporting and evidence generation production-grade
recommended_modifications.current_issue: The project has reporting capabilities, but reporting should be resilient and legally defensible in compliance scenarios.
recommended_changes: Version and sign generated reports to prevent tampering.
Store report output with metadata: generation time, model version, camera details, and data snapshot ID.
Add export controls for PDF/DOCX and digital signatures where required.
Allow review and approval flows before reports are considered final.
Keep original raw event data accessible for audit investigation.
acceptance_criteria: Every report is traceable to a specific session and evidence set.
Reports are tamper-resistant and attributable to a generation event.
Compliance review teams can audit the exact evidence behind each score.

recommended_modifications.title: Design for multi-site and multi-farm scale, not just a single deployment
recommended_modifications.current_issue: The platform appears optimized for a single operational setting; real scale requires tenancy, data separation, and resource governance.
recommended_changes: Introduce farm and site abstractions above the session abstraction.
Allow a single deployment to serve multiple farms with isolated data partitions or tenancy boundaries.
Add per-site configuration for camera IDs, detection thresholds, and staff roles.
Implement resource quotas and load balancing for site-specific workloads.
Build a data retention policy per site and region.
acceptance_criteria: The deployment can safely host multiple sites with isolation and resource limits.
Session and data queries stay correct even in a multi-tenant environment.
Admin operations can segment visibility by site and role.

recommended_modifications.title: Codify architecture, runbooks, operational ownership, and support model
recommended_modifications.current_issue: The project has good docs, but production readiness requires explicit ownership, runbooks, and support responsibilities.
recommended_changes: Create architecture decision records (ADRs) for major choices: streaming design, ML approach, event model, auth strategy, deployment model.
Publish operator runbooks for common incidents and camera issues.
Define support ownership by service: app, stream, ML, data, deployment.
Maintain a release checklist and rollback matrix.
Document maintenance procedures for model retraining and threshold tuning.
acceptance_criteria: A new engineer can operate the system without tribal knowledge.
Operational runbooks exist for all high-risk failures.
Architecture decisions are explicitly recorded and reviewed.

implementation_phases.name: Security and compliance hardening
goals: Add security headers and audit trails

critical_decisions_before_production: Decide whether the system will support a single farm with multiple cameras or multiple farms/tenant sites.
Define the official model strategy: custom-trained CV model, hybrid model, or rule-based fallback plus human review.
Choose the production deployment platform and observability stack.
Agree on the operational support model and who owns production incident response.
Clarify the legal/compliance requirements for audit evidence and report integrity.
key_success_metrics: < 1% data corruption events in task history
99.9% session health visibility during business hours
Task precision and recall meeting farm-approved SLA
Mean time to detect and resolve production incidents below target threshold
Zero critical security incidents in production rollout
final_recommendation: The project is already far beyond a toy system and has the right overall shape for a real production monitoring product. The highest-value next moves are to stabilize runtime orchestration, harden the event and data model, strengthen ML validation, and add meaningful production observability. Those changes will convert this from a promising platform into a deployable, auditable, and operationally reliable system.
